s1.syndrome_frame: pruritic skin lesions with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory findings
salient_findings: pruritic lesions on arms and legs
right-sided headache, sinus pain, and congestion
key_facts: patient is a 75-year-old black woman
patient has insulin-dependent diabetes
patient has obesity
patient presented with a 10-day history of pruritic lesions
patient has a 2-3 month history of night sweats
patient has a 3-week history of right-sided headache, sinus pain, and congestion
skin lesions developed while patient was taking prednisone
patient has no associated fever, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, myalgia, or arthralgia
patient has dozens of 1-2 cm oedematous pink-red papules with a darker red-violet central zone
patient has about 20 red macules on the medial aspect of her feet and the tips of her fingers and toes
patient has one 2 mm erosion on the soft palate of her mouth
white blood cell count is 2.7 × 10⁹/L
haemoglobin is 100 g/L
platelet count is 129 × 10⁹/L
absolute neutrophil count is 1.4 × 10⁹/L
liver function tests are normal
urinalysis shows 2+ protein, no blood
PCR for herpes simplex virus, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody, and cryoglobulins is negative
antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody is negative
IgA levels are elevated at 8860 mg/L

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic skin lesions with vascular damage and leucocytoclasia

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: atypical papular target lesions and mucosal involvement

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: fever, night sweats, and pruritic skin lesions with neutrophilic infiltrate

shortlist.label: IgA vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: elevated IgA levels and skin lesions with vascular damage

shortlist.label: Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic skin lesions with vascular damage and small-vessel involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of pruritic lesions, night sweats, and headache, along with the skin biopsy findings of atypical mononuclear cells and vascular damage, are consistent with Sweet syndrome. The elevated IgA levels and the presence of myeloperoxidase-positive cells also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has vasculitis, the clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with Sweet syndrome.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: The patient's lesions do not have the typical targetoid appearance of erythema multiforme, and the presence of atypical mononuclear cells is not typical of this condition.

rejected.label: IgA vasculitis
rejected.why: The patient's age and clinical presentation are not typical of IgA vasculitis, which is more commonly seen in children.

rejected.label: Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has small-vessel vasculitis, the clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with Sweet syndrome.
